answer: Identity is issued only after a day of live telemetry: the applicant stations a uniquely serialized instrument in a staffed grove, and that unit must emit a signed pulse every few minutes to a rotating coastal beacon whose location is posted at dawn. The ledger admits the name only once independent mast receipts and a one-time challenge-response line up. A replayed recording fails the nonce, and cloning is expensive because every extra identity needs its own powered instrument, distinct radio fingerprint, and beacon-visible uptime—copying one feed cannot staff a second grove.
